anomalies.observed: The +5V rail (the net fed by D1 from the external 5V jack J7 and feeding D2/servo rail and the PortB breakout J6) is tied to pin 25 of both M5Stack bus connectors J1 and J2. Pin 27 of J1/J2 carries the generic pass-through net labelled 'PIN27' instead.
anomalies.expected: Per the design specification, the +5V rail must be tied to J1/J2 pin 27, which is the M5Stack bus 5V pin; pin 25 should carry its normal M5Stack bus signal, not the board's +5V rail.

evidence.quote: The same `+5V` net is also tied directly to J1/J2 pin 27 (the M5Stack bus's 5V pin), so `+5V` is effectively the logical OR of 'M5Stack-supplied 5V' and 'external 5V input via D1'.
J2 / J1 pin row 25 is labelled `+5V`; pin row 27 is labelled `PIN27`; pin row 29 is labelled `BAT`.

anomalies.impact: The board's +5V rail is no longer tied to the M5Stack's 5V output: with only the M5Stack supplying power (no external 5V on J7), the servo rail (D2/C1-C4, J3/J8 pin 2) and the J6 PortB +5V are unpowered. At the same time the +5V rail is merged with M5Stack bus pin 25, which on the M5-Klis bus is not a 5V pin (it is the adjacent GND/GPIO-area pin), so the 5V rail is effectively shorted to that bus line when the board is stacked.

parsed.summary: The drawing deviates from the specification in the M5Stack bus 5V connection: the board's +5V rail is tied to J1/J2 pin 25 instead of the specified pin 27, so the M5Stack's 5V output is not routed to the board's 5V/servo rail (and +5V is instead merged with the bus line on pin 25). All other checked items (component values, D1 direction, R3/R4/R9-R15 values, TXD2/RXD2 and PWM jumper pin numbers) agree with the specification.
